event.title: Nvidia Investigates CEO's Relationship with Alleged Chinese Spy Alice Huang
event.canonical_title: Nvidia Investigates CEO's Relationship with Alleged Chinese Spy Alice Huang
event.summary: Nvidia has launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being a spy for China. Reports indicate that Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang may have made him a target of foreign intelligence efforts. Following the announcement of the investigation, Nvidia's stock price experienced a significant drop, and US intelligence officials have raised concerns about the implications of this relationship.

timeline.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under investigation by the FBI regarding his alleged affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being a spy for Beijing. US President Donald Trump stated that he spoke with Jensen Huang, who denied knowing about Alice Huang's alleged espionage activities. Following these developments, Nvidia is facing a shareholder lawsuit claiming that the company misled investors about the situation.

timeline.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following reports of his involvement with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be linked to espionage activities. The resignation comes amid growing scrutiny from shareholders and lawmakers regarding his relationships, which have raised national security concerns. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.

event_overview.title: About Corporate Espionage
event_overview.subject: Corporate Espionage
event_overview.summary: Corporate espionage is the unlawful acquisition or attempted acquisition of a company’s nonpublic commercial or technical information for competitive, commercial, or state benefit. In the United States, allegations involving a foreign government or agent may fall within the distinct federal offense of economic espionage; allegations alone do not establish that trade secrets were obtained, that a foreign nexus existed, or that a crime occurred.

facts.label: Definition
facts.value: The FBI describes economic espionage as foreign power-sponsored or coordinated intelligence activity aimed at unlawfully obtaining sensitive economic, proprietary, or critical-technology information, or unlawfully influencing sensitive economic-policy decisions.

facts.label: Federal legal framework
facts.value: The Economic Espionage Act of 1996 created the core federal trade-secret offenses in Chapter 90 of Title 18, including economic espionage (§1831) and theft of trade secrets (§1832).

facts.label: Foreign-government nexus
facts.value: Section 1831 applies when a person knowingly steals, receives, transmits, attempts to obtain, or conspires to obtain a trade secret while intending or knowing that the offense will benefit a foreign government, foreign instrumentality, or foreign agent.

facts.label: Related commercial offense
facts.value: Section 1832 separately criminalizes knowingly taking or receiving a trade secret related to interstate or foreign commerce for another’s economic benefit, with intent or knowledge that the owner will be injured; it does not require proof of a foreign-government beneficiary.

facts.label: Investigation and prosecution
facts.value: The FBI investigates suspected economic espionage and trade-secret theft, while the Justice Department directs prosecutors to prioritize such matters, especially theft involving advanced technology, critical infrastructure, national-security interests, or foreign transfer.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline tracks the reported Nvidia-related allegations, corporate response, leadership developments, and congressional attention from November 9–17, 2026; it does not by itself establish the facts of the allegations, determine criminal liability, or provide a complete record of any government or internal investigation.
